author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Scenario corpus of JSA/TRA analyses built from spec 15 (MVP scope, rules, acceptance criteria), spec 00-common (insufficient data must not look safe, unsupported configuration handled explicitly) and the hierarchy of controls in ISO 45001:2018 clause 8.1.2 (as quoted by a secondary source), NIOSH and HSE. Every risk matrix is supplied as an input profile (sizes, product/sum rule, inclusive band upper limits), so no published matrix value is assumed. Covers: complete analysis, determinism and re-scoring after a profile change, band edges on both sides of each limit for product and sum rules on square and non-square 2..10 scales, invalid matrices, out-of-range and missing ratings, residual traceability (no control / planned / unverified / vague / untagged / explanation override / credited / higher / equal / mixed), PPE-only flag on both sides of the High threshold, weak-control heuristics (owner, verification, spec's 'be careful' example), duplicate hazard/control wording versus linking, action register, missing header/step/hazard data, step-count 5-20 boundaries, a 30-step/100-hazard case and 10 randomized analyses (seed 20260916) whose scores, bands, used residuals, distributions and action registers come from ref.py. Inputs are tool-neutral: 'key' values are local handles the harness maps to tool IDs; empty string or null means left blank; status is 'in_place' or 'planned'.
reference_citations: ISO 45001:2018 Occupational health and safety management systems - Requirements with guidance for use, clause 8.1.2 'Eliminating hazards and reducing OH&S risks' (hierarchy a) eliminate ... e) adequate PPE); text as quoted at https://blog.auditortrainingonline.com/blog/iso-45001-clause-8-1-2 (primary text paywalled, not read directly)
NIOSH, Hierarchy of Controls, https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/hierarchy-of-controls/about/index.html (order elimination > substitution > engineering > administrative > PPE; PPE least effective)

HSE, Managing risks and risk assessment at work - steps needed to manage risk, https://www.hse.gov.uk/simple-health-safety/risk/steps-needed-to-manage-risk.htm (PPE last; record who carries out the action and by when)

tools.petrov.re spec 15 JSA/TRA Builder (MVP scope, 'Model, rules and checks', 'Validation and QA', acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common (insufficient data / review required; explicit negative scenarios)
tolerance: All checks exact. Scores are integers from integer ordinal ratings (product or sum), bands, flags and verdict states are categorical, and distributions/action registers are integer counts or key sets (compared as sets). The spec states the score is an ordinal index, not a probability, so no numerical tolerance other than identity is meaningful. Check names containing hazard[K]/control[K] refer to the input keys. 'verdict_state' uses the README verdict classes (insufficient / blocking / no_blocking_finding); 'verdict_is_no_blocking_finding: false' accepts any non-clear verdict.
